This is an experiment in mathematical exposition. The webpage displays the opening of the book Synthetic category theory by Denis-Charles Cisinski, Bastiaan Cnossen, and Tashi Walde. The webpage also contains an Agda formalization of this part of the book. The reader has the option to display the book and the Agda code side-to-side. Clicking an underlined passage in the text reveals the corresponding Agda code. Clicking a line in the Agda code causes the book to jump to the closest match in the text.

About this experiment

This experimental site is maintained by Bastiaan Cnossen. It has been built using substantial AI assistance, model Codex 6 Astra. My coauthors are aware of the experiment, but they do not necessarily endorse it; responsibility for this site rests with me alone, at least for now. In particular, I take the sole responsibility for the usage of AI for creating this site; no inference about my coauthors' opinion on AI should be inferred from this.

All mathematics on this webpage not in the form of Agda code is taken directly from the tex source of our joint book, extracted via a python script. Any error introduced by the conversion is mine. Edits to the book do not automatically result to changes to this webpage unless the python script is rerun, and so this webpage may not always display the up-to-date version of the book.

All Agda code on this webpage is AI generated. Some of the high-level naming conventions were chosen by me, but apart from that all implementation decisions were made by Codex.

Given the experimental nature of this webpage, I wish to mostly keep this webpage under the radar for now. The reason this is a public repository is only because GitHub Pages requires a public repository on a free plan.
